questions.question: A multi-step form loses data on navigation, a deep link 404s, or refresh breaks the router — what's the diagnosis?
questions.title: Forms Routing Scenarios
questions.direct_answer: Three classic scenario families: (1) MULTI-STEP FORM DATA LOSS — steps stored in component state die on route change (route remount resets it); fix by lifting the model to a route-context/store above all steps, or persisting to search params (useSearchParams — the URL becomes the state, survives refresh AND back/forward) — draft-in-URL is the durable pattern. (2) INVALID DYNAMIC ROUTE IDs — the param exists but references nothing: fetch-by-id must handle not-found as a UI state, and validate before render-gating (redirect to a list with a message rather than rendering an empty detail). (3) REFRESH 404s ON CLIENT ROUTES — the server only knows /index.html; /dashboard/settings 404s because the server looks for that FILE. Fix: server rewrite/fallback to index.html (SPA fallback on every host) so the client router takes over any path; the same answer for deep links.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    SYM{symptom} -->|step data vanishes on Next| L[step state scoped to its route mount]
    L --> F1['lift to context/store above the wizard route OR search params']
    SYM -->|deep link to junk id| P[param is any string — no guarantee]
    P --> F2[three-state UI: loading / not-found / content]
    SYM -->|refresh 404 on client route| S[server has no such file — no fallback]
    S --> F3[SPA fallback: serve index.html for every route — host config, not React]
    URL['URL-as-state: refresh-safe, shareable, back-button-friendly'] -.preferred for.-> F1
```

sections.title: Deep Dive
sections.content:
Why search params are the professional default for wizard/filter state (the full argument): they're the ONLY state that survives refresh, is shareable (copy/paste a link that reconstructs the view), works with back/forward as undo, and crawlers can read. The pattern: replace searchTerm/page/filters/step with useSearchParams, and derive everything from them — the component becomes a pure function of the URL. The costs worth naming: every param change re-renders + re-fetches (debounce search), params are strings (parse/validate at the boundary like any external input), and large blobs don't belong in URLs (store by key server-side).

The deeper multi-step architecture (when a wizard is a real feature): the state machine view — steps aren't pages, they're nodes in a flow graph with validation gates between them (step-complete = its schema passes; navigation allowed = current gate green). RHF + zod per step, with the wizard model accumulating partial schemas (merge each step's parsed output), gives you resume-anywhere for free because each step's data is valid when captured. Persist the model under a single storage key (localStorage/sessionStorage with a version stamp) and the wizard survives tab close — the uncontrolled-but-typed hybrid most production wizards converge on.

The router/SSR reconciliation (the forward-looking close): Next.js and remix-style routers move the fallback discussion server-side — file-based routing means the SERVER knows every route, so refresh-404s disappear structurally (no fallback needed; unknown routes are real 404s the framework renders). Client React Router remains for SPAs and embedded widgets. The interview-worthy arc: 'client router + fallback config' is the SPA answer; 'the framework owns the route table' is the meta-framework answer — know which one the codebase is before reaching for either fix.
